questionText:
Read the passage and answer the question:

Gandhiji on the Indian Elite

When his turn came to speak, Gandhiji charged the Indian elite with a lack of concern for the labouring poor. The opening of the BHU, he said, was “certainly a most gorgeous show”. But he worried about the contrast between the “richly bedecked noblemen” present and “millions of the poor” Indians who were absent. Gandhiji told the privileged invitees that “there is no salvation for India unless you strip yourself of this jewellery and hold it in trust for your countrymen in India.” “There can be no much spirit of self-government about us,” he went on, “if we take away or allow others to take away from them almost the whole of the results of their labour. Our salvation can only come through the farmer. Neither the lawyers, nor the doctors, nor the rich landlords are going to secure it.” Gandhiji’s speech at Banaras in February 1916 was, at one level, merely a statement of fact – namely, that Indian nationalism was an elite phenomenon, a creation of lawyers and doctors and landlords.

The central idea of the passage is:

questionText:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Alongside political agitations, Mahatma Gandhi consistently emphasized his 'Constructive Programme' including Hindu-Muslim unity, abolition of untouchability, and promotion of Khadi.
Statement II: Gandhi considered political Swaraj completely meaningless unless social inequalities and caste untouchability were simultaneously eradicated from Indian society.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Erroneously assumed both statements were valid.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Rejected valid scientific statements erroneously.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize the fallacy in Statement II.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Statement I is false while Statement II is factually sound.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
1. Statement I is correct: Gandhi devoted years between agitations to constructive work.
2. Statement II is correct: For Gandhi, true Swaraj required moral transformation and eradication of social oppression.
Hence, Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Hence Option C is correct.
Hence, option (D) is correct.
